title: Prefetch router for quantization-aware microbatch scheduling
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Introduce a lightweight Prefetch Router that makes runtime kernel routing decisions for incoming requests based on quantization compatibility, prefix cache hits, and per-request latency SLOs. The router will also prefetch dequantized KV slices and group compatible requests into microbatches that allow overlap between dequant work and attention prefill/kv-copy, reducing end-to-end p95 token latency for quantized execution paths (INT8/FP8).

Why now: We observe a significant dequant overhead for short-response workloads and high-frequency chat traffic when using INT8/FP8 kernels. Current execution serializes dequant + attention prefill, which increases scheduler stalls and wastes GPU kernel launch windows. A routing + prefetch layer can (a) reduce dequant tail latency by overlapping work, (b) prefer slightly larger microbatches when SLOs allow to amortize dequant cost, and (c) fall back to native FP32 kernels when prefix cache miss patterns suggest the overhead outweighs benefits.

Scope: Prototype in the runtime request path (hosted and dedicated) implementing three components: Router (fast decision logic), Prefetcher (KV slice staging and lightweight requantization buffer), and Microbatch Scheduler (temporal grouping with SLO-aware thresholds). This is an engineering-first change with a toggleable feature flag and telemetry to measure token-level latency and per-kernel utilization.

Success metrics (target):
- p95 token latency on conversational shorter-turn workloads down by 12-25% on INT8/FP8 routes versus baseline.
- GPU kernel utilization improvement of 7-15% for serving fleets with high short-turn traffic.
- No more than 1% regression in output correctness (verified by existing eval prompt sets) when using FP8 hybrid routes.

Out-of-scope: Full model-rewrite to support new quant formats or new quant-aware transformers. This ticket is focused on runtime orchestration and staging; kernel implementations remain unmodified (we use existing int8/fp8 kernels).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Router decision path implemented and behind feature flag. 2) Prefetcher correctly stages KV slices and dequant buffers with instrumentation. 3) Microbatch scheduler groups compatible requests without violating per-request latency SLO config. 4) End-to-end automated regression tests pass (latency, correctness, and throughput). 5) Performance benchmarks demonstrating >=12% p95 latency improvement on benchmark harness for short-turn chat workload. 6) Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads.
tasks: Implement Router API for per-request metadata and decision cache
Implement Prefetcher shim to stage KV slices asynchronously to pinned buffers
Add Microbatch Scheduler with configurable grouping window and SLO knobs
Integrate telemetry: per-token latency, kernel type, dequant time, queueing time
Unit + integration tests: correctness for INT8/FP8 fallbacks
Benchmark: run chat-short-turn harness on LLaMA-2-13B quantized models
Rollout: canary on 2% traffic, monitor, then ramp to 25% / 100%
Docs: runtime changelog and feature flag usage
benchmark_results: Preliminary lab run (2026-02-28) on LLaMA-2-13B quantized profile: p95 token latency baseline 84ms -> router+prefetch 68ms (19% improvement) for 1-3 token replies; throughput at 2x microbatch size increased by 11%. Repro runs scheduled in CI.
risks: 1) Incorrect prefetching may increase memory pressure on pinned buffers and evict useful KV cache entries. 2) Aggressive grouping may violate tight latency SLOs for premium customers. 3) FP8 numerical edge cases may surface new correctness regressions. 4) Telemetry noise could hide regressions if not granular enough.
mitigations: Memory cap and LRU eviction for staging buffers; SLO-aware conservative defaults; run eval prompt sets (existing QA harness) on canary before ramp; add histogrammed telemetry and per-route alerting.
rollback_criteria: Increase in customer-facing p95 > 5% for routes with the feature enabled OR >2% increase in eval failure rate on the regression suite triggers immediate rollback to feature-off for that tenant. Automatic rollback hooks documented in runtime-ops playbook.

notes: Implementation choices considered: (A) push dequant into separate worker threads (adds cross-stream copies) vs (B) prefetch staging in pinned device memory to allow in-place overlap. We selected (B) because it minimizes inter-thread synchronization and can reuse existing kernel API for in-place inputs. We will reevaluate if memory pressure is higher than forecasted.
